source.title: Breakfast Time
source.description: Nombra alimentos del desayuno y distingue lo que comemos de lo que bebemos.

grammar.explanation: Usamos «I eat» para decir qué alimento comemos y «I drink» para decir qué bebida tomamos. Después ponemos el nombre del alimento o la bebida. En esta misión practicamos las dos frases como modelos completos.
grammar.model: I eat toast. I drink milk.
grammar.practice: Clasifica los alimentos del desayuno y completa la frase con eat o drink.

items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence for milk.
items.es: La leche es una bebida: usamos drink.

items.prompt: Complete: I ___ toast.
items.es: Toast es comida: usamos eat.

items.prompt: Complete: I ___ juice.
items.es: Juice es una bebida: usamos drink.

items.prompt: Choose the sentence about an egg.
items.es: Un huevo es un alimento; el modelo usa eat.

source.readingText: It is Saturday morning. Mia is in the kitchen with Mum and Leo. Mia has cereal and milk for breakfast. Leo has toast and an egg. There is orange juice on the table. Mum has yogurt. Mia drinks milk and Leo drinks juice. They smile and say, “Good morning!”

readingQuestions.question: When is the family having breakfast?
What does Leo have with his toast?
What juice is on the table?
What do they say in the morning?

source.listeningScript: Mum: Good morning, Sam. It is breakfast time. Sam: Good morning, Mum. I eat toast. Mum: Would you like milk? Sam: No, thank you. I drink juice. Mum: Here is an egg. Sam: Thank you. Mum: And here is yogurt for later. Sam: Great! I like breakfast.

listeningQuestions.question: What time of day is it?
What food does Mum give Sam?
How does Sam feel about breakfast?

source.title: At the Café
source.theme: Pedir alimentos y bebidas de forma guiada
source.description: Reconoce fórmulas de cortesía y practica pedidos muy sencillos en una cafetería.

pronunciation.activity: Escuchar el sonido inicial y repetir
Practicar las vocales y repetir
Marcar las sílabas al decir la palabra
Escuchar el sonido final y repetir

grammar.explanation: En un pedido sencillo podemos decir el nombre de la bebida o comida y añadir «please» para pedirla con educación. Cuando recibimos algo, podemos responder «thank you». En esta misión practicamos estas expresiones como fórmulas completas.
grammar.practice: Construye un intercambio corto entre una persona que pide y otra que sirve.

items.prompt: You want water. What do you say?
items.es: Añadimos please al pedido.

items.prompt: The café worker gives you a sandwich. What do you say?
items.es: Thank you sirve para dar las gracias.

items.prompt: Choose the polite request.
items.es: El nombre de la bebida + please forma el pedido.

items.prompt: Complete the exchange: “Tea, please.” “___”
items.es: Después de recibir lo que pedimos, damos las gracias.

source.readingText: At the café, Ben is with his sister. Ben says, “Water, please.” His sister says, “Juice, please.” The café worker brings water and juice. They sit at a small table. Ben has a sandwich and his sister has tea. They smile and say, “Thank you!”

readingQuestions.question: Where are Ben and his sister?
What does his sister ask for?
Which polite word do they use to ask?
What do they say after the worker brings the drinks?

source.listeningScript: Presenter: Welcome to our little café programme. Today we are listening to a simple order. Customer: Tea, please. Worker: Of course. Customer: Thank you. Worker: Would you like a sandwich? Customer: Yes, please. Presenter: The customer has tea and a sandwich. Remember: say please when you ask and thank you when you receive something.

listeningQuestions.question: What programme are we listening to?
What drink does the customer order first?
What polite word does the customer use?
Does the customer want a sandwich?
What does the customer say after the tea?
What two things does the customer have?
What should we say when we receive something?

grammar.focus: What is it? It is a…
grammar.explanation: Usamos «What is it?» para preguntar qué animal es. Para responder, decimos «It is a…» y el nombre del animal. Con algunos animales usamos «an», pero en esta misión el modelo principal es «a duck».
grammar.model: What is it? It’s a duck.
grammar.practice: Escucha o lee una pista y responde con “It is a…” más el animal.

items.prompt: Choose the correct question.
items.es: What is it? pregunta qué es.

items.prompt: Complete: What is it? It is ___ cow.
items.es: Cow empieza con sonido consonántico; usamos a.

items.prompt: Choose the correct answer for a duck.
items.es: El modelo usa It is + a + animal.

items.prompt: You hear “quack”. Which animal is it?
items.es: Quack es el sonido que se asocia al pato en esta misión.

source.readingText: At the farm, Lily hears a sound. “Moo!” It is a cow. Then she hears “quack, quack!” It is a duck. A sheep is near the gate. A horse is in the field. A pig is by the tree and a chicken is near the barn. Lily asks, “What is it?” and names each animal.

readingQuestions.question: Which animal is near the gate?
Which animal is by the tree?
Which animal is near the barn?
Which animal makes a sound twice in the text?

source.listeningScript: Host: We are at the farm with Alex. Alex, what can you hear? Alex: Moo! Host: What is it? Alex: It is a cow. Host: And now? Alex: Quack, quack! It is a duck. Host: Can you hear the sheep? Alex: Yes. Baa! Host: What about the horse? Alex: The horse is next to the field. Host: Thank you, Alex!

listeningQuestions.question: Who is at the farm with the host?
What sound does Alex hear first?
What animal makes the first sound?
What sound does Alex hear next?
What sound is linked to the sheep?

grammar.explanation: «There is…» significa «hay» cuando hablamos de una cosa o un animal. Después ponemos «a» y un nombre singular: «There is a cow». En esta misión reconocemos la frase completa; no hace falta crear todavía frases largas.
grammar.model: There is a cow on the farm.
grammar.practice: Escoge la imagen que coincide con una frase que empieza por “There is…”.

items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
items.es: There is se usa aquí para una sola vaca.

items.prompt: Complete: There ___ a hen.
items.es: Para un solo animal usamos There is.

items.prompt: What does “There is a sheep” mean?
items.es: There is presenta una cosa o un animal.

items.prompt: Choose the phrase for one goat.
items.es: Goat está en singular; usamos a goat.

source.readingText: Tom visits a farm with his grandad. The farmer is near the barn. There is a cow in the field. There is a sheep next to the barn. A goat is by the gate and a hen is near the farmer. Tom looks at the animals and says, “There is a busy farm!”

readingQuestions.question: Which animal is in the field?
Which animal is next to the barn?
Which animal is near the farmer?
What does Tom see on the farm?
What does Tom say about the farm?

source.listeningScript: This is a story about a farm. Emma is with the farmer. First, she looks at the barn. There is a cow in the field. There is a sheep near the barn. Emma sees a goat by the gate. A hen is next to the farmer. Emma says, “I like the farm. I can see many animals.”

listeningQuestions.question: What does Emma look at first?
Which animal is by the gate?
Which animal is next to the farmer?
What kind of text is the audio?

writingSource.text: There is a cow on the farm.
writingSource.translation: ahí EI a vaca encendido el finca.

grammar.focus: It is a…; nombres de animales en singular
grammar.explanation: Para nombrar un animal podemos decir «It is a…» y después su nombre: «It is a fish». Usamos «a» delante de la mayoría de estos nombres; delante de «octopus» usamos «an»: «It is an octopus».
grammar.model: It is a shark. It is a whale.
grammar.practice: Lee la frase y señala el animal marino correcto.

items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
items.es: El modelo es It is + a + animal.

items.prompt: Complete: It is ___ octopus.
items.es: Octopus empieza con sonido vocálico; usamos an.

items.prompt: Choose the sentence about a turtle.
items.es: Turtle comienza con sonido consonántico; usamos a.

items.prompt: What does “It is a whale” name?
items.es: La frase nombra un animal marino.

source.readingText: At the aquarium, Lily sees a fish first. A shark swims in a big tank. A whale is in the next picture. She likes the dolphin because it jumps. There is an octopus near a rock. A crab walks on the sand and a turtle swims slowly. Lily loves the sea animals.

readingQuestions.question: Which animal does Lily see first?
Which animal is near a rock?
Which animal is in the next picture after the shark?
What kind of animals does Lily love?

source.listeningScript: Guide: Welcome to the aquarium. Look at the fish. Visitor: I can see it. Guide: Now look at the shark. It is big. Visitor: And what is that? Guide: It is a whale. Here is a dolphin. It can jump. Visitor: I can see an octopus, too. Guide: Yes, and there is a crab near the rock. The turtle is in the blue tank.

listeningQuestions.question: Which animal does the guide ask the visitor to look at first?
What animal is shown after the shark?
Which animal does the visitor also see?

grammar.explanation: Usamos «Look for…» para decir «busca…» y «Find…» para indicar «encuentra…». El verbo va en su forma básica y la frase puede terminar con el nombre del pequeño animal.
grammar.model: Find a bee. Look for a butterfly.
grammar.practice: Lee la instrucción y elige el insecto que tienes que buscar.

items.prompt: Choose the correct instruction.
items.es: En un imperativo usamos el verbo base: find.

items.prompt: What does “Look for a butterfly” mean?
items.es: Look for significa buscar.

items.prompt: Complete: ___ an ant.
items.es: La instrucción empieza con el verbo base Find.

items.prompt: Choose the instruction for a spider.
items.es: La forma de instrucción es Look for + animal.

source.readingText: It is a sunny day in the garden. Ella has a little bug hunt card. First, she finds an ant near a leaf. Then she sees a bee on a flower. A butterfly flies over the grass. There is a spider under a leaf. A red ladybird is on a plant, and a green caterpillar is next to it. Ella smiles.

readingQuestions.question: Which small animal is on a flower?
Which animal is described as green?
How does Ella feel at the end?

source.listeningScript: Presenter: Welcome to the garden bug hunt. Are you ready? First, find an ant. It is near a stone. Now look for a bee on a flower. Can you see a butterfly? It is over the grass. Look under the leaf. There is a spider. Find the ladybird on the plant. And look next to it. There is a caterpillar. Well done, bug hunters!

listeningQuestions.question: Where does the bug hunt take place?
Which animal is next to the ladybird?
What does the presenter say at the end?

grammar.explanation: Para nombrar y describir un animal, usamos «It is a…» y podemos añadir un adjetivo antes del nombre: «a big elephant». El adjetivo va antes del animal.
grammar.practice: Elige el adjetivo y el animal que coinciden con la descripción.

items.es: El adjetivo big va antes del nombre elephant.

source.readingText: At the zoo, Leo visits the animals with his class. The lion is big. The tiger is orange and black. A tall giraffe eats leaves. An elephant drinks water. A monkey climbs a tree. The zebra has black and white stripes. A bear is near the rocks. Leo likes the giraffe best.

readingQuestions.question: What stripes does the zebra have?
Which animal does Leo like best?

source.listeningScript: Interviewer: Hello, Maya. What can you see at the zoo? Maya: I can see a lion. It is big. Interviewer: What is next? Maya: A tiger. It is orange and black. Interviewer: Can you see the giraffe? Maya: Yes. It is tall. And there is an elephant. It is very big. Interviewer: Which animal do you like? Maya: I like the monkey. It is funny!

listeningQuestions.question: Which animal does Maya see first?
How does Maya describe the lion?
How does Maya describe the giraffe?
Which other very big animal does Maya see?
How does Maya describe the monkey?

source.title: Where Is It?
source.description: Localiza objetos en una escena usando preposiciones de lugar muy frecuentes.

pronunciation.activity: Escuchar el sonido inicial y repetir
Practicar las vocales y repetir

grammar.focus: Preposiciones: in / on / under / next to
grammar.explanation: Las preposiciones indican dónde está un objeto. «In» es dentro de; «on» es sobre; «under» es debajo de; «next to» es al lado de; «behind» es detrás de; «in front of» es delante de. Observa el objeto y el lugar antes de elegir.
grammar.model: The ball is under the table.
grammar.practice: Coloca un objeto según la frase y reconoce su posición.
grammar.order: The ball is under the table.
final: The ball is under the table.
The ball under is the table.
The table is under the ball.

items.prompt: The book is ___ the bag. It is inside.
items.es: In indica que el libro está dentro de la bolsa.

items.prompt: The cup is ___ the table. It touches the top.
items.es: On indica que está sobre la superficie.

items.prompt: The cat is ___ the chair. It is below it.
items.es: Under significa debajo de.

items.prompt: The ball is ___ the box. It is beside it.
items.es: Next to significa al lado de.

source.readingText: In the playroom, the red ball is in the box. A book is on the table. The cat is under the chair. A blue bag is next to the table. The teddy bear is behind the door. A toy car is in front of the chair. Can you find every object?

readingQuestions.question: Which object is inside the box?
Which animal is in the playroom?
How many objects are named in the text?
Where does the story take place?

source.listeningScript: This is a story about a tidy room. A little ball is in a box. A book is on the table. A cat is under the chair. The school bag is next to the table. Look behind the door. There is a teddy bear. A toy car is in front of the chair. Now the room is easy to see!

listeningQuestions.question: Which object is in the box?
What helps us find each object?
How is the room at the end?

writingSource.text: The ball is under the table.
writingSource.translation: el bola EI bajo el mesa.

grammar.explanation: Usamos «he» para hablar de un hombre o un niño y «she» para hablar de una mujer o una niña. Para nombrar a un familiar podemos decir «my mother» o «my grandfather». Cuando hablamos de varias personas juntas, podemos reconocer «they».
grammar.model: She is my mother. He is my father.
grammar.practice: Relaciona cada familiar con He is o She is. Usa They are cuando hables de varias personas.

items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about a mother.
items.es: She se usa para hablar de una mujer.

items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about a father.
items.es: He se usa para hablar de un hombre.

items.prompt: Complete: ___ is my sister.
items.es: Sister es hermana; usamos she.

items.prompt: You talk about your mother and father. Choose the pronoun.
items.es: They se usa para hablar de dos o más personas.

source.readingText: This is my family photo. My mother is Ana and my father is Luis. My sister is Eva. My brother is Tom. The baby is my little brother. My grandmother and grandfather are in the photo too. They are happy. I love my family.

readingQuestions.question: Who else is in the photo?
How are the family members in the photo?
Who is the text speaker talking about?
What does the speaker say at the end?

source.listeningScript: Teacher: Hello, Sam. Who is in your family photo? Sam: This is my mother. She is Ana. Teacher: And who is he? Sam: He is my father, Luis. This is my sister, Mia, and this is my brother, Ben. Teacher: Are they your grandparents? Sam: Yes. They are my grandmother and grandfather. Teacher: Thank you, Sam.

listeningQuestions.question: Who is showing the family photo?
What does Sam say about the grandparents?
listeningQuestions.answer: They are his grandmother and grandfather
options: They are his grandmother and grandfather

listeningQuestions.question: How many people are named in the photo?
